subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should non-local device-less WebSocket clients authenticated with a shared token/password be allowed to retain operator scopes, and should that be the default or an explicit token-scope policy?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally preserve scopes only for narrow local paths, while the report and related PRs ask to broaden remote token-auth behavior on a Gateway auth boundary.

options.title: Default-safe token-scope policy
options.body: Keep remote device-less scope clearing as the default and land an explicit configured token-scope mechanism for trusted headless deployments.

options.title: Restore remote token retention
options.body: Treat valid shared token/password auth as enough for non-local WebSocket operators to retain requested scopes by default, accepting the broader security boundary.

options.title: Close as unsupported remote device-less use
options.body: Document that remote WebSocket operator clients must pair or use a supported token-scope configuration instead of retaining self-declared scopes.

recommendation.title: Default-safe token-scope policy
recommendation.body: Keep remote device-less scope clearing as the default and land an explicit configured token-scope mechanism for trusted headless deployments.
